<?php
const MOD = 1000000007;

fscanf(STDIN, "%d %d", $w, $h);

$N = ($w + 1) * ($h + 1);
$N_mod = $N % MOD;

$total_ordered_triples_mod = 1;
$total_ordered_triples_mod = ($total_ordered_triples_mod * $N_mod) % MOD;
$total_ordered_triples_mod = ($total_ordered_triples_mod * (($N - 1) % MOD)) % MOD;
$total_ordered_triples_mod = ($total_ordered_triples_mod * (($N - 2) % MOD)) % MOD;

$colinear_sum_mod = 0;

$term_h = ($w + 1) % MOD;
$term_h = ($term_h * ($h + 1) % MOD) % MOD;
$term_h = ($term_h * $h % MOD) % MOD;
$term_h = ($term_h * ($h - 1) % MOD) % MOD;

$term_v = ($h + 1) % MOD;
$term_v = ($term_v * ($w + 1) % MOD) % MOD;
$term_v = ($term_v * $w % MOD) % MOD;
$term_v = ($term_v * ($w - 1) % MOD) % MOD;

$colinear_sum_mod = ($term_h + $term_v) % MOD;

$max_d = min($w, $h);
for ($dx = 1; $dx <= $max_d; $dx++) {
    for ($dy = 1; $dy <= $max_d; $dy++) {
        if (gcd($dx, $dy) != 1) continue;
        
        if ($dx > $w || $dy > $h) continue;
        
        $num_segments = (($w - $dx + 1) * ($h - $dy + 1)) % MOD;
        $k_minus_1 = ($dx - 1) * ($dy - 1);
        $term = (2 * $num_segments) % MOD;
        $term = ($term * $k_minus_1) % MOD;
        $colinear_sum_mod = ($colinear_sum_mod + $term) % MOD;
    }
}

$non_degenerate_mod = ($total_ordered_triples_mod - $colinear_sum_mod + MOD) % MOD;

$cnt_x[0] = (int)(($w + 2) / 2);
$cnt_x[1] = ($w + 1) - $cnt_x[0];
$cnt_y[0] = (int)(($h + 2) / 2);
$cnt_y[1] = ($h + 1) - $cnt_y[0];

$freq = [];
for ($px = 0; $px < 2; $px++) {
    for ($py = 0; $py < 2; $py++) {
        $freq[$px][$py] = ($cnt_x[$px] * $cnt_y[$py]) % MOD;
    }
}

$total_even_d_mod = 0;
for ($px1 = 0; $px1 < 2; $px1++) {
    for ($py1 = 0; $py1 < 2; $py1++) {
        for ($px2 = 0; $px2 < 2; $px2++) {
            for ($py2 = 0; $py2 < 2; $py2++) {
                for ($px3 = 0; $px3 < 2; $px3++) {
                    for ($py3 = 0; $py3 < 2; $py3++) {
                        $v = ($px1 * $py2 + $px2 * $py3 + $px3 * $py1 - $px2 * $py1 - $px3 * $py2 - $px1 * $py3) % 2;
                        if ($v < 0) $v += 2;
                        if ($v == 0) {
                            $prod = $freq[$px1][$py1];
                            $prod = ($prod * $freq[$px2][$py2]) % MOD;
                            $prod = ($prod * $freq[$px3][$py3]) % MOD;
                            $total_even_d_mod = ($total_even_d_mod + $prod) % MOD;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

$sub_E_mod = 0;

$e_x = $cnt_x[0] % MOD;
$o_x = $cnt_x[1] % MOD;
$e_y = $cnt_y[0] % MOD;
$o_y = $cnt_y[1] % MOD;

$S0 = ($e_x * $e_y) % MOD;
$S1 = ($e_x * $o_y) % MOD;
$S2 = ($o_x * $e_y) % MOD;
$S3 = ($o_x * $o_y) % MOD;

$S_sum = ($S0 + $S1 + $S2 + $S3) % MOD; // N
$S_sq_sum = ($S0 * $S0 + $S1 * $S1 + $S2 * $S2 + $S3 * $S3) % MOD;

$term1 = (3 * $S_sq_sum) % MOD;
$term1 = ($term1 * (($N - 2) % MOD)) % MOD;

$term2 = 2;
$sum_S_cu = 0;
foreach ([$S0, $S1, $S2, $S3] as $s) {
    $sum_S_cu = ($sum_S_cu + $s * $s % MOD * $s) % MOD;
}
$term2 = ($term2 * $sum_S_cu) % MOD;

$term3 = (6 * $S0 % MOD * $S1 % MOD * $S2) % MOD;
$term4 = (6 * $S0 % MOD * $S1 % MOD * $S3) % MOD;
$term5 = (6 * $S0 % MOD * $S2 % MOD * $S3) % MOD;
$term6 = (6 * $S1 % MOD * $S2 % MOD * $S3) % MOD;

$sub_E_mod = ($term1 - $term2 - $term3 - $term4 - $term5 - $term6) % MOD;
if ($sub_E_mod < 0) $sub_E_mod += MOD;

$total_E_distinct_mod = ($total_even_d_mod - $sub_E_mod + MOD) % MOD;

$answer = ($non_degenerate_mod + $total_E_distinct_mod) % MOD;
$answer = ($answer * 500000004) % MOD; // Modular inverse of 2

echo $answer . "\n";
?>

source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: In a single output line print an integer — the remainder of dividing the answer to the problem by 1000000007 (109 + 7).
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: A single line contains two integers w and h (1 ≤ w, h ≤ 4000).
source_data.prob_desc_description: The Little Elephant is playing with the Cartesian coordinates' system. Most of all he likes playing with integer points. The Little Elephant defines an integer point as a pair of integers (x; y), such that 0 ≤ x ≤ w and 0 ≤ y ≤ h. Thus, the Little Elephant knows only (w + 1)·(h + 1) distinct integer points.The Little Elephant wants to paint a triangle with vertexes at integer points, the triangle's area must be a positive integer. For that, he needs to find the number of groups of three points that form such triangle. At that, the order of points in a group matters, that is, the group of three points (0;0), (0;2), (2;2) isn't equal to the group (0;2), (0;0), (2;2).Help the Little Elephant to find the number of groups of three integer points that form a nondegenerate triangle with integer area.
